FileData.description: What was recorded from a file, as FileDataIn took it.
FileData.title: FileData

FileDataIn.description:
What was read from the file, as the extract workflow records it: the document type and version it was
read as, whether a template or the model read it, how many fields wait for a person, and the extraction. A file read
with Detect whose kind is none of the team's types has no type and no version: it was not recognised.
FileDataIn.title: FileDataIn

FileList.description: A page of files, the counts of each view the Files page offers, and facet counts, all from the query.
FileList.title: FileList

FileRow.description: A list row: the file record without versions and references.
FileRow.title: FileRow

FileSource.description:
Where a file from a watched folder came from: the watch (its name is None once the watch is deleted), its path
at the source, when the source last changed the version Files holds, when the source stopped listing it, and its
access list as last read. `access_list` None means the source never said; [] means it lists nobody. The list is
recorded, not applied (exception E58).
FileSource.title: FileSource

Folder.description:
One picked place of a watch: the input it was picked for, the source's id, and the name the picker showed
(the id when none was kept).
Folder.title: Folder

LastCheck.description:
What the last check ended as: success, partial, refused or failed, with what it brought in and why it
stopped; `failures` names the first failed files.
LastCheck.title: LastCheck

Option.description:
One choice in a picker: what it stores, what it shows, a short hint, and why it cannot be chosen when it
cannot (the agent lacks a tool the widget needs, say).
Option.title: Option

OptionsPage.description:
A page of a picker's choices, searched and limited in the store query. `next_cursor` asks for the next page;
None at the end. Every `/options` route answers this, and `ids=` resolves stored values to their labels.
OptionsPage.title: OptionsPage

ReadRequest.description: A read request and the system extract run it started, once the event was delivered.
ReadRequest.title: ReadRequest

ReadRequestIn.description:
Read the file with a team's document type, the newest version when none is named; with no type, the file
is classified over the team's types and read with the one found (Detect).
ReadRequestIn.title: ReadRequestIn

StorageDocument.description: A saved document, as StorageDocumentIn took it.
StorageDocument.title: StorageDocument

StorageTarget.description: A saved target, as StorageTargetIn took it.
StorageTarget.title: StorageTarget

StorageTargetIn.description: Where one purpose's bytes go. `default` covers every purpose without its own target.
StorageTargetIn.title: StorageTargetIn

WatchEvents.description: Events after `after`, oldest first; `next_after` asks for the next page, None at the end.
WatchEvents.title: WatchEvents

get.description: This service's background processes and their state; counts and error types only, no record's data.

Available files of the caller's team on the shared list contract, newest first (`sortBy` name, uploadedAt,
size, scan or purpose; equal values stay newest first); `uploadedBy=me` keeps the caller's own. Search, the
uploaded dates, the view and the purpose, scan, sensitivity, read-as type and read path filters run in the
query, which also answers each view's count and the facet counts; `readPath=model` keeps files no template
matched. The filters are declared here so a bad value is refused; ListQuery reads the same keys as its
filters.

A service names the person it writes for in `uploadedBy`; a person is always the uploader.
